title: 'Which is Better' card A/B test: photo-top card vs full-bleed photo card with overlay
attribution_visible_in_image: Footer credit 'Abraham John @ui.abraham' and header 'Design Testing 00'. Likely the author; not confirmed. The upload filename ('Framer Portfolio Website Design') does not match the content.

observed.layout: A 'design testing' poster: serif headline 'Which is Better' (second word lighter) over a graph-paper grid with a rounded frame; two phone-shaped cards labeled A and B in white circles. A: rounded photo on top with a bookmark button on the photo, name 'Natasha Romanoff' with a blue verified badge, two-line bio, a three-stat row (4.8 Rating, $45k+ Earned, $50/hr Rate) with dividers, and a black full-width 'Get In Touch' with a mail icon. B: photo fills the card with a dark gradient overlay and white text, the same stats, and a CTA row with a white 'Get In Touch' pill and a separate dark bookmark button. Footer: author avatar and 'Abraham John @ui.abraham' at left, 'Save for later' with a bookmark icon at right.
observed.hierarchy: Headline, then the two cards, then the A/B labels.
observed.typography: High-contrast serif display for the headline; neutral sans in the cards. Unconfirmed.
observed.iconography: Mail and bookmark icons; verified badge; star in the rating.
observed.materials: A: white card with rounded photo. B: full-bleed photo with gradient overlay.

implementation_notes: B overlay: gradient from transparent to near-black behind the text block.
Bookmark moves from the photo (A) into the CTA row (B).
Stats use dividers in both variants.
interpretation.caveat: Inference. The A/B change is not a single variable: photo treatment, text color, CTA color and bookmark placement all differ.

concept_work.essence: Present two treatments of one card side by side and ask which communicates better.
what_makes_it_work: Identical content and framing make the comparison fair at a glance.
Both variants measure comfortably high contrast.
gaps_to_make_it_work: More than one variable changes between A and B, so the 'test' is confounded.
No hypothesis or success metric is stated.
B's bio legibility depends on the overlay depth.

links: The footer 'Save for later' echoes the bookmark action inside the cards.
A and B share content so differences are attributable to treatment.

approach: Same component with two layout modes

pattern.name: A/B presentation with a stated variable
use_when: Communicating a design decision or comparing treatments
avoid_when: The variants differ in many ways and no metric is given
adaptation_examples: Pricing page test: same plans, different emphasis.
Onboarding test: same steps, different layout.

lessons: Change one variable per variant when comparing designs.
Put the unit in the stat value ('$50/hr').
open_questions: Was there a result or metric?

related.relation: same stat triple (rating, earned, rate) with units

measured.palette_method: Median-cut quantization of the supplied image plus saturated-pixel hue medians. Approximate (JPEG). Items marked 'approx' were judged by eye.
measured.color_roles: Neutral graph-paper stage; color comes from the photo; black/white CTA flips between variants.
measured.contrast_method: Estimated from compressed images. Background = dominant color in a box around the text. ratio_low = conservative estimate (mean of the most distant ~4% of pixels). ratio = best estimate (mean of the most distant ~1.5% of pixels; for text on a saturated background that appears near-white or near-black, the text is assumed pure white or black, because anti-aliasing of small text otherwise understates the contrast). Accessibility scores use ratio_low; critical failure CF1 uses ratio. Gradient or photo backgrounds are measured one text line at a time. Values within 0.4 of a threshold are borderline and should be verified in the source file.

evidence: A clear comparison post built around a contact card.
Elegant staging with a serif headline and graph-paper grid; both cards read well.
Card conventions and equal framing are respected; the confounded variables are noted but do not break the card itself.
Single CTA, bookmark and stats are clear in both variants.
A and B share structure, radii and type.
Comparison-post format is familiar; the overlay card is standard.
Scored on conservative values: primary text min 15.16:1; secondary text min 7.05:1; icon min n/a:1; non-color state cue: True.
accessibility.basis: computed from measured contrast + cue flag (scope: contrast and non-color cues only; touch targets, motion and screen-reader support cannot be assessed from a static image)

evaluation.readiness_key: A = ship with minor adjustments (>=80, no critical failure); B = needs specific fixes (60-79); C = rethink (<60)
evaluation.scope: Scored as presented in a static image. States, motion and behavior that are not shown are not scored as present.
